lit.\u0027Aportan resistencia a la tracción,: "They provide tensile strength, anchor the nucleus and the organelles and form the nuclear lamina."
lit.\u0027Complejo de ADN enrollado en histo: "Complex of DNA wound on histones. Less compact (euchromatin, active) or very compact (heterochromatin). When the cell divides it condenses into chromosomes."
lit.\u0027Complejo de unas 30 proteínas dist: "Complex of about 30 different proteins with octagonal symmetry that crosses the nuclear envelope."
lit.\u0027Dan forma, sirven de «carreteras»: "They give shape, serve as “highways” for vesicle transport (kinesin and dynein) and form the mitotic spindle, cilia and flagella."
lit.\u0027Dan resistencia mecánica, permiten: "They give mechanical strength and enable cell movement, phagocytosis, cytokinesis and microvilli. In plants they take part in cytoplasmic streaming."
lit.\u0027Digieren macromoléculas, bacterias: "They digest macromolecules, bacteria and old organelles (autophagy). They recycle cell components."
lit.\u0027Doble capa de fosfolípidos (cabeza: "Double layer of phospholipids (hydrophilic heads outward and hydrophobic tails inward) with cholesterol (in animals) and integral and peripheral proteins. It is the “fluid mosaic”."
lit.\u0027Doble hélice de monómeros de actin: "Double helix of actin monomers; they form a network under the membrane (cell cortex)."
lit.\u0027Empaqueta el ADN y regula qué gene: "It packages the DNA and regulates which genes are read; when the cell divides it condenses to distribute the genetic material."
lit.\u0027En el hígado degradan buena parte: "In the liver they degrade a good part of the alcohol we consume."
lit.\u0027En el hígado el retículo liso es a: "In the liver the smooth reticulum is abundant because alcohol and medicines are metabolized there."
lit.\u0027Envoltura de dos membranas continu: "Envelope of two membranes continuous with the endoplasmic reticulum, perforated by nuclear pores. It contains chromatin, nucleolus and nucleoplasm."
lit.\u0027Es muy abundante en células secret: "It is very abundant in secretory cells, such as those that produce antibodies or digestive enzymes."
lit.\u0027Es muy viscoso y está lleno de mol: "It is very viscous and full of molecules: more a “thick soup” than a free liquid."
lit.\u0027Es tan delgada que se necesitarían: "It is so thin that about 10,000 stacked membranes would be needed to match the thickness of a sheet of paper."
lit.\u0027Guarda el ADN y regula la expresió: "It stores the DNA and regulates gene expression; DNA replication and transcription (RNA synthesis) take place there. It controls the activities of the cell."
lit.\u0027Junto con la miosina producen la c: "Together with myosin they produce muscle contraction."
lit.\u0027Las células que fabrican muchas pr: "Cells that make a lot of protein have large nucleoli or several."
lit.\u0027Las plantas con flores no tienen c: "Flowering plants have no centrioles and organize their spindle in other ways."
lit.\u0027Los cromosomas solo tienen forma d: "Chromosomes are only “X”-shaped during division; the rest of the time the chromatin is dispersed."
lit.\u0027Membrana externa lisa y membrana i: "Smooth outer membrane and inner membrane folded into cristae that surround the matrix, where there are mitochondrial DNA and ribosomes of their own."
lit.\u0027Modifica, clasifica y empaqueta pr: "It modifies, sorts and packages proteins and lipids into vesicles; it completes glycosylation and directs them to the membrane, the lysosomes or the exterior."
lit.\u0027Organizan los microtúbulos y forma: "They organize the microtubules and form the mitotic spindle to distribute the chromosomes during division."
lit.\u0027Oxidan ácidos grasos largos y deto: "They oxidize long fatty acids and detoxify substances; catalase breaks down hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) into water and oxygen."
lit.\u0027Par de centriolos perpendiculares: "Pair of perpendicular centrioles (9 triplets of microtubules) surrounded by pericentriolar material."
lit.\u0027Partículas de ARN ribosomal y prot: "Particles of ribosomal RNA and proteins made of two subunits (60S and 40S). They can be free in the cytosol or attached to the rough reticulum."
lit.\u0027Pequeñas burbujas de membrana que: "Small membrane bubbles formed by budding from other compartments."
lit.\u0027Pila de sacos aplanados con una ca: "Stack of flattened sacs with a cis face (receives vesicles from the reticulum) and a trans face (sends them out). "
lit.\u0027Producen la mayor parte del ATP me: "They produce most of the ATP through cellular respiration (Krebs cycle, respiratory chain and oxidative phosphorylation)."
lit.\u0027Pueden crecer y acortarse en segun: "They can grow and shorten in seconds (dynamic instability)."
lit.\u0027Recibe el nombre de Camillo Golgi,: "It is named after Camillo Golgi, who described it in 1898 by staining neurons with silver nitrate."
lit.\u0027Red de cisternas aplanadas continu: "Network of flattened cisternae continuous with the nuclear envelope, with ribosomes attached to its cytosolic face (“rough” appearance)."
lit.\u0027Red de túbulos ramificados sin rib: "Network of branched tubules without ribosomes, continuous with the rough one."
lit.\u0027Región densa dentro del núcleo, fo: "Dense region inside the nucleus, made of ribosomal DNA, ribosomal RNA and proteins."
lit.\u0027Regula el tránsito núcleo ↔ citopl: "It regulates nucleus ↔ cytoplasm traffic: mRNA, tRNA and ribosomal subunits go out; histones, transcription factors and enzymes come in."
lit.\u0027Sede de reacciones metabólicas com: "Site of metabolic reactions such as glycolysis and of cytosolic protein synthesis; the medium through which molecules diffuse and vesicles move."
lit.\u0027Según la teoría endosimbiótica, de: "According to the endosymbiotic theory, they descend from bacteria that were taken in by ancestral cells."
lit.\u0027Separa el interior del exterior y: "It separates the inside from the outside and controls what enters and leaves (selective permeability): channels, transporters, pumps, endocytosis and exocytosis. It receives signals through receptors."
lit.\u0027Si estirases todo el ADN de una cé: "If you stretched out all the DNA of a human cell it would measure ~2 m, and it fits in a nucleus a few microns wide."
lit.\u0027Sintetiza el ARN ribosomal y ensam: "It synthesizes ribosomal RNA and assembles the ribosome subunits, which then leave through the nuclear pores."
lit.\u0027Sintetiza lípidos (fosfolípidos, e: "It synthesizes lipids (phospholipids, steroids), detoxifies drugs and poisons and, in muscle, stores calcium."
lit.\u0027Sintetiza proteínas destinadas a l: "It synthesizes proteins destined for secretion, the membrane and lysosomes/vacuoles; it folds them and adds initial carbohydrates (glycosylation)."
lit.\u0027Solución gelatinosa, ~70–80 % agua: "Gel-like solution, ~70–80 % water, with ions, metabolites, proteins, enzymes and free ribosomes. Together with the organelles it forms the cytoplasm."
lit.\u0027Son los más estables del citoesque: "They are the most stable of the cytoskeleton; keratins make up hair and nails."
lit.\u0027Su pH ácido protege al resto de la: "Their acidic pH protects the rest of the cell: if they break, the enzymes hardly act in the cytosol (pH ≈ 7.2)."
lit.\u0027Traducen el ARN mensajero en prote: "They translate messenger RNA into proteins. Free ones make proteins for the cytosol, nucleus, mitochondria and chloroplasts; attached ones make those that are secreted or go to membranes."
lit.\u0027Transportan moléculas entre orgánu: "They transport molecules between organelles and toward the membrane (exocytosis) or from it (endocytosis)."
lit.\u0027Tubos huecos de tubulina α y β.\u0: "Hollow tubes of α and β tubulin."
lit.\u0027Un núcleo típico tiene miles de po: "A typical nucleus has thousands of pores and each one can transport hundreds of molecules per second."
lit.\u0027Una célula en crecimiento puede te: "A growing cell can have millions of ribosomes."
lit.\u0027Una sola neurona puede liberar mil: "A single neuron can release thousands of vesicles with neurotransmitters in seconds."
lit.\u0027Vesículas con oxidasas y catalasa;: "Vesicles with oxidases and catalase; often with a dense crystalline core."
lit.\u0027Vesículas con unas 50 enzimas hidr: "Vesicles with about 50 hydrolytic enzymes that work at acidic pH (~5)."
